answer: Each agent can earn transfer rights only after staking a scarce token and completing a useful task that another agent accepts; disputes slash the stake. A newcomer can create a thousand identities, but each must lock capital and risk losing it, while splitting one stake across identities does not multiply their earning capacity. The zephyr of cheap account creation therefore cannot wash over the ocean of real economic weight: scaling a Sybil attack means buying and risking more stake, not just generating names on a ridge.
